    The nondistributive case of Theorem 3.14 #

    A split basic algebra B whose lattice of two-sided ideals is not distributive has a quotient Λ = B/K with a socle pair (Bongartz, Corollary 2); the quotient construction F₁ over Λ gives the data of Theorem 5.2 (Lemma 3.4, Proposition 4.1), and inflation along B → Λ transports it to B.

    TopOneDim k (S.e x)

    In a split basic algebra every Λ e_x / J e_x is one-dimensional.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.exists_jacobson_list_prod {k : Type u} [Field k] {Λ : Type u} [Ring Λ] [Algebra k Λ] [FiniteDimensional k Λ] :
    ∃ (n : ℕ), ∀ (l : List Λ), l.length = n → (∀ j ∈ l, j ∈ Ring.jacobson Λ) → l.prod = 0

    The Jacobson radical of a finite-dimensional algebra is nilpotent, in the form of products of n radical elements.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.jacobson_pow_finrank {k : Type u} [Field k] {Λ : Type u} [Ring Λ] [Algebra k Λ] [FiniteDimensional k Λ] :
    Ring.jacobson Λ ^ Module.finrank k Λ = ⊥

    The Jacobson radical J of a finite-dimensional algebra satisfies J ^ d = 0 for d = dim Λ: the powers of J decrease strictly until they vanish.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.jacobson_list_prod_finrank {k : Type u} [Field k] {Λ : Type u} [Ring Λ] [Algebra k Λ] [FiniteDimensional k Λ] (l : List Λ) (hl : l.length = Module.finrank k Λ) (hJ : ∀ j ∈ l, j ∈ Ring.jacobson Λ) :
    l.prod = 0

    Products of dim Λ radical elements vanish.
